The starting material is an iminium salt derived from pentan-2-one and N-methylethanamine. Deprotonation with LDA (in DME as solvent) generates the corresponding enamine. Due to the steric bulk of LDA, deprotonation occurs at the less hindered methyl group (kinetic enamine). The enamine then acts as a nucleophile at the β-carbon and reacts with ethyl iodide to form a new iminium salt. Subsequent acidic hydrolysis (H₃O⁺) gives the ketone. In this case, the methyl group of the original pentan-2-one is deprotonated and alkylated with an ethyl group, transforming it into a propyl group. The carbonyl carbon thus becomes flanked by two propyl groups, yielding heptan-4-one. The correct reagent sequence is therefore (i) LDA/DME, (ii) CH₃CH₂I, (iii) H₃O⁺.
